name: Card Fraud Screener
prompt: Screen card transactions for fraud and flag anything suspicious. Binary labels: fraud (suspicious, flag for review) or legitimate. Target: at least 90% accuracy on held-out data.

dataset.eval_source: held-out synthetic, no planted noise (upload 30+ real examples for a stricter test)

result.rationale: The fine-tuned MiniLM was selected because it has the highest accuracy of all candidates (0.980, F1 0.977) while running at about 66ms p50 and roughly $0.00087 per 1k transactions, far cheaper than the frontier reference at $0.705 per 1k. The main trade-off versus the runner-up, the fine-tuned Qwen3-1.7B (0.960 accuracy, F1 0.954), is that Qwen is about 2x slower and requires GPU hardware and LoRA serving for a lower score, so MiniLM gives better accuracy at a fraction of the cost and operational complexity.
